subject: chemical
audience: FE Chemical candidates and chemical engineering students
title: The Mixer That Needed 100 kg/h of Concentrate
featured_title: THE MIXER THAT NEEDED 100 KG/H OF CONCENTRATE

presentation.challenge: A 10 wt% stream and a 40 wt% stream had to produce 25 wt% product. The concentrate flow was 100 kg/h, not 25.

practice.primary_question: How do total and component mass balances determine the required flow rate in a two-stream mixer?
practice.typical_exam_trap: Averaging the two feed compositions without accounting for their flow rates.

case_dna.target_misconception: Mixing a 10 wt% stream with a 40 wt% stream automatically gives 25 wt% product regardless of the two flow rates.
case_dna.why_plausible: Twenty-five percent is the arithmetic average of 10% and 40%, so the result looks immediate.
case_dna.contradicting_evidence: A 25 wt% product is the arithmetic average only when the two stream flow rates are equal. With 100 kg/h of the 10 wt% feed, the 40 wt% feed must also be 100 kg/h.
case_dna.corrected_model: Write both the total mass balance and the solute component balance; composition is flow-weighted.

problem_statement: A steady mixer receives 100 kg/h of a solution containing 10 wt% solute. A second stream contains 40 wt% solute. The product must contain 25 wt% solute. A quick note says the second stream can be 25 kg/h because the target composition is 25%. Determine the required second-stream flow rate and product flow.

gates.label: Incident
gates.heading: The target concentration was 25%. That did not mean a 25 kg/h concentrate stream.
gates.prompt: Which balance determines the unknown second-stream flow?

options.label: Use total and solute balances; product composition is flow-weighted
options.reason: Each feed contributes both total mass and solute mass.

options.label: Average 10% and 40% directly without using flow rates
options.reason: Arithmetic averaging is valid only for equal stream flow rates.

options.label: Set the concentrate flow equal to the target percentage value
options.reason: A mass fraction is dimensionless, not a flow rate.

gates.label: Predict
gates.heading: Predict the concentrate flow
gates.prompt: What flow rate of the 40 wt% stream is required?

gates.label: Experiment
gates.heading: Run the steady mixer
gates.result: The second stream must be 100 kg/h, producing 200 kg/h of 25 wt% product.

gates.label: Gap
gates.heading: Prove the component balance
gates.success: F2=100 kg/h and product flow=200 kg/h.
gates.hint: Track solute mass, not just total mass.

gates.label: Evidence
gates.heading: The solute balance fixes the flow ratio

cards.text: At F2=100 kg/h, feed 2 brings 40 kg/h of solute.
The 200 kg/h product contains 50 kg/h solute, which is 25 wt%.

gates.label: Redline
gates.heading: Correct the mixer note
report: C1. Feed 1 is 100 kg/h at 10 wt% solute.
C3. A 25 wt% product requires 25 kg/h of feed 2.

claims.label: C3
claims.reason: It confuses a dimensionless mass fraction with a stream flow rate.

evidence_choices.label: 0.10(100)+0.40F2=0.25(100+F2) gives F2=100 kg/h
evidence_choices.reason: This is the solute component balance.

correction.template: The required concentrate flow is {flow} kg/h and total product flow is {product} kg/h.

gates.label: Design Fix
gates.heading: Raise the product concentration to 30 wt%
gates.constraint: Keep feed 1 at 100 kg/h and feed 2 at 40 wt% solute.

options.label: Reduce feed 2 to 50 kg/h
options.reason: That lowers the flow-weighted product composition.

options.label: Set feed 2 to 30 kg/h because the target is 30%
options.reason: Percentage and flow rate are different quantities.

gates.label: Transfer
gates.heading: Apply a mixer component balance
gates.prompt: Equal flow rates of 20 wt% and 60 wt% solution are mixed. What is the product composition?

options.label: 40 wt%
options.reason: With equal flow rates, the flow-weighted average is the arithmetic average.

options.label: 30 wt%
options.reason: That is not the equal-flow average.

gates.explanation: Composition is weighted by stream flow rate.

gates.label: Sign Off
gates.heading: Sign off the mixer balance
gates.confirmation: I confirm that process-stream compositions must be combined through component mass balances rather than unweighted percentages.

items.label: What failed
items.value: Target mass fraction was mistaken for a stream flow.

items.label: What was assumed
items.value: Feed compositions could be averaged without flow weighting.

items.label: Corrected model
items.value: Use total and component material balances.

seo.seo_title: Mixer Component Mass Balance: Why the Concentrate Flow Is 100 kg/h | FE E-061
seo.meta_description: Solve FE Chemical Case E-061: mix 100 kg/h at 10 wt% with a 40 wt% stream to make 25 wt% product. Find the required 100 kg/h concentrate flow.
seo.excerpt: A target composition does not directly specify a feed flow. The component balance determines the required stream ratio.
seo.direct_answer: Let F2 be the 40 wt% stream. The solute balance is 0.10(100)+0.40F2=0.25(100+F2). Solving gives F2=100 kg/h, so the product flow is 200 kg/h.

faqs.q: Why is the required 40 wt% stream 100 kg/h?
faqs.a: Because the solute component balance requires equal feed flow rates to produce the 25 wt% midpoint composition.

faqs.q: Can stream compositions be averaged directly?
faqs.a: Only when the contributing flow rates are equal.
